svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.10.9.9 Penetrations by Raceways, Sprinklers and Fire Dampers
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Penetrations by Raceways, Sprinklers and Fire Dampers

g.text: Combustible totally enclosed raceway in a slab
at least 50 mm (1 15/16″) of concrete below it
Totally enclosed raceway through a fire separation
sealed by a firestop to Clause 9.10.9.6.(1)(a)
Sprinkler piping through a fire separation
permitted where both fire compartments are sprinklered
no firestop where a metal escutcheon plate covers
Fire damper in a steel sleeve
Fire damper: no firestop needed where
installed to NFPA 80, designed with a firestop,
House with a secondary suite: a noncombustible
duct with all openings serving one fire

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Combustible totally enclosed raceways embedded in a concrete floor
slab are permitted in a rated assembly
Provided the concrete cover between the raceway and the bottom of the
slab is not less than 50 mm (1 15/16″).
Totally enclosed raceways may penetrate a fire separation if sealed
by a firestop conforming to Clause 9.10.9.6.(1)(a)
Sprinkler piping may penetrate a fire separation if the fire
compartments on each side are sprinklered
Sprinklers may penetrate a fire separation or a rated membrane
without the firestops of Article 9.10.9.6. and Clause
Provided the annular space is covered by a metal escutcheon plate in
accordance with NFPA 13, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler
Systems".
Fire dampers may penetrate a fire separation or a rated membrane
without the firestops of Sentence 9.10.9.6.(1), provided the damper
is
(a) installed in conformance with NFPA 80, "Standard for Fire Doors and
Other Opening Protectives", (b) specifically designed with a firestop, or
(c) provided in conformance with Sentence 9.10.5.1.(3). See also Note
In a house with a secondary suite, including its common spaces,
ducts penetrating fire separations need not have fire dampers in
conformance with Article 3.1.8.10.
Provided they are noncombustible with all openings in the duct system
serving only one fire compartment.
Fire, smoke and combination smoke/fire dampers are intended to be
installed to Subsection 3.1.8., Sentence 3.1.9.1.(5) and their listing
and labelling, which may or may not permit firestopping around the duct.
Drawn: close-ups, cut to show the parts. Red: fire separations. Orange: firestop. Blue: combustible raceway. Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.9.9. (page 9-69)
